title: First Floor Group Study Rooms
description: The Library has several rooms reservable for groups of two to ten people equipped with white boards perfect for your study session.
image-alt: three students collaborate around a table

title: First Floor Instruction Room
description: Located on the first floor of the Library, the Instruction Room is a space equipped with tables, rolling chairs, and an instructor station with seating for 30 students. This space is perfect for evening workshops, co-curricular groups, and large study groups. This room must be reserved eight hours in advance.
image-alt: a group of students in a classroom with tables

title: Third Floor Individual Study Rooms
description: The Library has two individual study rooms that can be reserved and six that are available on a first-come, first-served basis. All feature a desk and a chair, perfect for working by yourself. Ask for help at the Circulation Desk if you need help finding your room!
image-alt: a desk with notebook and laptop

title: Open Group Study Rooms
description: Six group study rooms are available for general use on a first-come, first-served basis. Rooms include 309, 308, 322, and 321 on the Third floor, and 414 and 415 on the Fourth floor. They contain three to seven chairs with space appropriate for small groups. Please tidy up when you are finished using the rooms and do not "camp out" for extended periods of time.
image-alt: three students collaborate around a table

title: EHHS Team Rooms
description: The Education, Health and Human Services building has four Team Rooms available by reservation or on a first come first serve basis. Reservations must be made a day in advance by contacting the Gary Strong Curriculum Center at curriculumcenter@uidaho.edu. Located on the second and fourth floors of the College of Education, Health, and Human Sciences building (rooms 215, 217, 415, 417), the rooms are equipped with two white boards and a TV monitor, with a max capacity of nine people. Great for collaborating with classmates and/or colleagues.
image-alt: three students collaborate around a table

title: The Studio
description: Located on the Library's first floor, the Studio offers dedicated space to UI-affiliated students, staff, and faculty to record, edit, or digitize audiovisual content. Faculty and staff can capture high-quality lectures and instructional videos using the eGlass and other equipment. Students, staff, and faculty can use the Studio to support their teaching, learning, and creative pursuits at the University of Idaho. Visit the Studio homepage for more information.
image-alt: a person recording audio at a computer workstation

title: 3D Printers
description: The Library's two LulzBot TAZ Workhorse 3D printers are located in the MILL (Making Innovating and Learning Laboratory) on the first floor of the Library and can be reserved to print your project. Visit the MILL's website for full information.
image-alt: a person watching a 3D printer at work

title: Glowforge
description: The MILL has a Glowforge with an attached filtration unit. This amazing machine can cut and engrave acrylic, wood, and vegetable-tanned leather. The Glowforge can be reserved by U of I students, staff, and faculty. Users are responsible to bring in their own materials from our approved list.
image-alt: Laser cutting device on a desk

title: Graduate Study Carrels
description: The Library has six rooms reservable by graduate students. These rooms include a desk, chair, and shelf and can be reserved for semesters at a time. For more information, to reserve a study carrel, or to be added to the wait list, please email libcirc@uidaho.edu.
image-alt: a desk with bookshelf and books

title: Tabling @ the Library
description: The Library has space available for tabling on the first floor or directly outside the main entrance. Tabling is open to U of I student and university groups. Please submit requests for tabling at least one week in advance, so we may review our events calendar.
image-alt: a welcome table with handouts and displays
